The product \((x-1) f(x)\) has degree \(1 + \deg(f)\). The right-hand side is \(3x^4 + x^3 - 25x^2 + 38x - 17\), which is a polynomial of degree \(4\). Therefore, \(1 + \deg(f) = 4\), so \(\deg(f) = 3\). Moreover, substituting \(x=1\) into the right-hand side gives \(0\), confirming that \(x-1\) is a factor and the quotient \(f(x)\) is indeed a polynomial of degree \(3\).

Answer: 3
